context:
Goal: reviews end, and a small fix stays cheap.
Problem (rule): rule roles-review-cap-three says a failed fix check starts a new lane at round 1. That also resets the three-round cap, so fail, fix, fail could loop forever, and a one-line slip costs a whole fresh review.
Based on (read): CLAUDE.md rule roles-review-cap-three, its last sentence; incident #1420 (the Windows fix), 13:03 CST.
Departs from: main, where a failed fix check restarts at round 1 in a new lane — a counts it as the next round within the cap; c adds one more fix check.

options.gain: The cap really caps, and a slip needs no new lane.
options.label: A failed fix check counts as the next review round, inside the three-round cap (recommended)
options.lose: A slip uses up one of the three rounds.

options.label: Keep it as it is
options.lose: The cap can be dodged, and small slips are expensive.

options.label: Allow one more fix check before any full round
options.lose: Weaker: a second fix check reads only the fix.

reply: a, saved 13:12 CST. Sent to the coordinator: a failed fix check counts as the next review round, inside the three-round cap. Rule roles-review-cap-three is rewritten to say so.
short: Failed fix check: next round, or start over?
title: Should a failed fix check count as the next review round, instead of starting over at round 1?
why: You asked in chat at 13:07 CST: "is it a good idea that i have it built this way that it resets the run or nah".
